biography.plain_text: Born in Issoudun, Bruno Joyerot is a French businessman who built a group of leather-goods manufacturers serving luxury fashion houses. A gift from his parents supplied Groupe Mada's initial capital. He acquired Arco and expanded production in western France, assembling other specialist workshops through Yeraz before selling several of them to Chanel.

long_biography.plain_text:
Bruno Joyerot delayed construction of Arco's new leather-goods factory until he could fund the project without disrupting employees' profit-sharing payments. He enlarged the plans to give staff more comfortable working space as orders and employment grew. The replacement factory opened in 2019 across from the older premises in Châtellerault.

In Saint-Barthélemy, two residents introduced Joyerot to cardiologist Yves Journo, whose online appeal for equipment had attracted little funding. Joyerot bought a cardiac ultrasound machine for the island's hospital. The donation allowed consultations to resume, giving the medical team a way to examine the heart and blood flow locally.
